question: How many metric tons of US soybeans will China have committed to for marketing year 2026/27, per the USDA Weekly Export Sales report covering the week ending October 1, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Verified base: China MY26/27 commitments were 9.855 MMT in the week ending 2026-09-10 (US total 20,631.4 TMT), with only ~0.33 MMT shipped. Three unobserved weeks remain. Recent observed China booking pace is ~0.875-1.0 MMT/wk, with a reported mid-September lull (Sept 18 flash of 111 kt was 'first in a few days'), and the Trump-Xi summit on Sept 24 falls inside the window and could unlock a burst or, if it sours, a stall. Central case ~3.0 MMT added over three weeks plus modest unknown-destination switches as harvest shipments ramp, landing near 12.8 MMT; I shade the median to ~12.55 because ~28% of my weight sits on the resolver using the Oct-2-published report, which covers the week ending Sept 24 (one week less of accumulation). Counterargument in the other direction: 2020-style pre/post-summit buying weeks of 2-3 MMT are on record, and 13 MMT of China-linked cargoes are already tracked by trade sources on a broader basis, so a 16 MMT+ print is live (3.5%). Downside below 8 MMT needs ~2 MMT of net cancellations, which accumulated exports and a live summit make near-impossible (1%). No human prediction market prices this contract.
sources: USDA FAS Weekly Export Sales, report released 2026-09-17 (data week ending 2026-09-10), via secondary quotation

NOT net weekly sales, NOT 'Unknown destinations', NOT other marketing years, NOT trade-press cargo counts, NOT calendar-year purchase tallies.

EVENT WINDOW: measurement date is the reporting week ending 2026-10-01 per the criteria; MY2026/27 began 2026-09-01, so the in-marketing-year portion of the window is 2026-09-01 -> 2026-10-01 (30 days), of which as of Now (2026-09-21T00:30Z) 20 days = 67% have elapsed. Note commitments also include forward bookings made before Sept 1 (new-crop sales ran from roughly June 2026). Published data currently extends only to the week ending 2026-09-10, i.e. 3 of the 5 reporting weeks between Sept 1 and Oct 1 are still unobserved as of Now.

PUBLICATION CADENCE: FAS releases the weekly report each Thursday 08:30 ET covering the reporting week ending the PRIOR Thursday (8-day lag). Oct 1 2026 is a Thursday. Therefore the release on Oct 1 2026 covers the week ending Sept 24; the week ending Oct 1 data publishes Oct 8 2026. The criteria's parenthetical 'the report published on or about October 2, 2026' does not match the week it names.

- Class 'reporting week nearest Oct 1, marketing years with normal Chinese buying (2016/17, 2017/18, 2020/21-2024/25)': China ESR commitments have historically fallen roughly in the 9-20 MMT band, with a central tendency around 12-13 MMT; the 2020/21 post-Phase-One year is the high outlier near 20 MMT. (Approximate, from historical ESR series; not re-verified from a primary pull this run.)
- Class 'same weeks, trade-war-blackout years (2018/19, 2019/20, 2025/26)': near zero to ~5 MMT. This year is NOT in that class — China is actively buying.
- Conditional class 'given the level at the week ending Sept 10 is known': weekly China net soybean sales during mid-September to early October in active-buying years have typically run on the order of 0.5-2.5 MMT per week, with occasional 3 MMT weeks in 2020.
- Mechanical anchor: 9.855 MMT observed + three unobserved weeks at the in-year observed run-rate.
- Additive channel beyond new sales: cargoes booked to 'Unknown destinations' are reallocated to China at or near shipment, raising China's commitment line without a corresponding flash sale. Cancellations/washouts move it the other way; accumulated exports cannot decline.

The Oct 1 figure therefore equals that anchor plus three unpublished weeks (w/e Sept 17, 24, Oct 1); total commitments move only with net sales, so rising shipments do not affect it. Documented pace is ~0.9-1.4 MMT/week from state buyers all summer, with Reuters reporting roughly 1 MMT taken in the Sept 14-18 week and 600k+ booked Sept 12-15, so the first of the three weeks is largely banked; 3 x ~1.0 gives ~12.9. Right skew comes from the Sept 24 Trump-Xi summit (a deal removing China's 10% retaliatory tariff would bring sidelined private crushers back) and from unknown-destination books being switched to China, a routine Sept-Oct occurrence. Left tail is bounded: a summit blow-up halts new buying but cannot unwind the already-transacted Sept 17 week, so realistic floor is ~11 MMT; sub-8 MMT needs ~2 MMT of mass cancellations, near-unprecedented. Small extra left weight reflects the risk a resolver uses the Oct 1-published report (week ending Sept 24, ~1 MMT lower) despite the criteria naming the Oct 1 week. Contradicting sources claiming China is 'past halfway' or at '13 MMT' appear to be calendar-2026 or unknown-destination-inclusive accounting: at 13 MMT for China, non-China MY26/27 commitments would be only 7.6 MMT, implausibly low, so the 9.85 USDA figure governs.

- A Chinese trade delegation was due in Washington the week of 2026-09-21.
- Late September/early October is the seasonal peak for Chinese bookings of US new crop; USSEC CEO Jim Sutter expects shipments to China to accelerate late Sept/early Oct as harvest gains momentum.
- Unknown-destination commitments are substantial and routinely get switched to China, which raises China's commitments without any new gross sale.

- Only state-owned buyers (Sinograin, COFCO) are active; private crushers remain out because the 10% tariff leaves US beans uncompetitive against Brazilian.
- Sinograin announced an auction of 543,000 MT of previously purchased beans from reserves on 2026-09-22, signalling ample near-term domestic supply.

- Both the US and Brazil are on record-crop paths for 2026/27.
- Buying is politically timed and lumpy — a summit disappointment could pause it.

Adjusting: the observed run rate is 0.88-1.22 MMT/week, Sinograin's ~1 MMT week of Sept 7-11 lands in the Sept 17 report, the Sept 24 Trump-Xi summit (possible removal of China's residual 10% soybean duty) is an upside catalyst for the Sept 25-Oct 1 week, and switches out of the large unknown-destinations balance can lift China's line without new sales; offsetting are lumpy SOE booking, a record Brazilian crop, harvest price pressure and Beijing's non-acknowledgement of the extra $17bn. Escapes: below 8 MMT requires ~1.9 MMT of net cancellations, which needs a summit collapse with mass washouts, ~1%; above 16 MMT requires +6.2 MMT in three weeks, above any three-week Chinese increment outside a 2020-scale frenzy, ~3.5%.

calls.reasoning: Hard anchor: FAS has China at 9,858,300 MT of MY2026/27 commitments for the week ending 2026-09-10, triangulated three ways and consistent with the 20.63 MMT all-destination total. The Oct 1 figure is that anchor plus three unpublished weeks (w/e Sep 17, Sep 24, Oct 1); commitments move only with net sales, so the shipment ramp reshuffles outstanding into accumulated without changing the sum. Observed weekly increments have been unusually stable at 0.87-1.22 MMT (mean 1.02), giving straight continuation near 12.9; the reference-class three-week increment of ~+2.9 MMT lands in the same place. I sit slightly above at 13.05 for three reasons: late Sep-Oct is the seasonal peak of Chinese new-crop booking, a ~4 MMT Unknown-destinations reservoir widely attributed to China switches onto the China line in lumps as Oct-Dec vessels are lined up, and the Sep 24 Trump-Xi summit sits inside the window with USTR signaling ag announcements and China's residual 10% duty (which keeps private crushers sidelined) the named candidate for relief. Counterweights are real but already priced into the 0.87 MMT Sep-10 print: Nov beans at $13.03 are dear against Brazil, traders flagged sales slowing on price, Sinograin is auctioning 543 kt of reserves, Chinese stockpiles are at multi-year highs, and SOE slot-booking is lumpy and politically timed. Market check: no human market prices this quantity - the harness found nothing on Polymarket or Manifold, and all four runs' independent checks found Kalshi listing soybean PRICE contracts only (its Apr-2026 ag event contracts were delisted) and no bookmaker line, so there is no crowd anchor to blend.
calls.reconciliation: Four runs, one shared evidence base, no material factual conflict on the anchor: China MY2026/27 commitments were 9,858,300 MT at week ending 2026-09-10, confirmed by arithmetic that closes three ways (8.983 + 0.8753 = 9.8583; 694 + 62.5 = 756.5 vs 758 mbu reported all-destination). Every run independently derived the FAS 8-day lag, so the question's parenthetical 'published on or about October 2' contradicts the reporting week it names - the week ending Oct 1 publishes Oct 8. I treat the named reporting week as binding (it appears in both the criteria and the fine print, and the fine print directs waiting for a delayed report rather than annulling) and carry ~18% on a resolver instead taking the report published Oct 1/2, which covers the week ending Sep 24 and would read roughly 1 MMT lower. That is materially less shading than Runs 1-3 applied (20-28%, with Run 1 at 28% dropping its median to 12.55) and is the single biggest reason my number sits above the pool's centre - I am not adding upside they missed, I am removing a discount I think they over-applied. The trade-press 'China is past halfway / 13 MMT' claims are settled against this instrument by Run 2's consistency check: at China = 13 MMT, all other destinations plus Unknown would be only 7.6 MMT of a 20.63 MMT total. Those figures run on a calendar-year and/or Unknown-inclusive basis. One factual dispute I could NOT settle without web access: whether Sinograin's Reuters-reported 14-15 cargoes (~1 MMT) are already inside the 875,300 MT week-ending-Sep-10 print (Run 1) or fall into the not-yet-published week ending Sep 17 (Run 3), and relatedly whether mid-September was a lull (Run 1's '111 kt was the first sale in a few days') or a ~1 MMT week (Run 2's Reuters read of Sep 14-18). The reporting week ending Sep 10 covers Sep 4-10, so a Sep-10-dated 'this week' story overlaps it heavily and Run 1's reading is the more likely one - but rather than resolve it by fiat I let the w/e Sep 17 increment carry the full 0.5-1.2 MMT uncertainty, which is part of why my p10 sits at 11.25 rather than tighter. I carry forward Run 3/Run 4's reference class (three-week mid-Sep-to-Oct-1 increment in active-buyer years, ~+2.9 MMT median) because it agrees with the bottom-up continuation figure of 3 x 1.02; note all four runs flagged these prior-year increments as reconstructed from pattern knowledge rather than pulled from the ESR archive, so the class is directionally right but not precisely measured, and my dispersion reflects that. Escapes: below 8 MMT requires ~1.9 MMT of net cancellation against a base that includes uncancellable accumulated exports - I keep a token 1% for a summit collapse with mass washouts or a large China-to-Unknown reallocation, siding with Runs 1-3 over Run 4's zero. Above 16 MMT requires 2.05 MMT/week for three weeks, which has precedent only in the 2020 post-Phase-One frenzy but has a concrete mechanism here (tariff removal plus mass Unknown-to-China switching), priced at 5% with Runs 2 and 4. Every FAS figure in this reconciliation is secondary trade-press recap - apps.fas.usda.gov returned 403 to all four runs - which is itself an argument for staying near the continuation anchor rather than reaching.

disagreements.verdict: Accepted as real (Runs 2/3/4). Unknown was ~3.8 MMT at Aug 13 and grew after; switches post as positive China net sales and cluster as Oct-Dec vessels are lined up. Sized as right skew, not as a shift in the median.

disagreements.claim: Whether the median belongs above or below straight continuation (~12.9 MMT)
disagreements.verdict: Above, with Run 4. Seasonal booking peak, the Sep 24 summit inside the window, and switch-lumpiness outweigh the price-competitiveness and Sinograin-reserve-auction counterweights, which are already reflected in the softer 0.87 MMT Sep-10 print.
